subject: Pilot results: per-annotator heads vs majority vote
body:
Hi both,

Pilot is trained, two days ahead of the 04-24 milestone. Numbers on the held-out Corpus hate-speech slice:

- Majority-vote baseline: F1 0.66
- Multi-annotator model (one head per annotator, NaN-masked where an annotator skipped an item): F1 0.71 when we aggregate heads, and we additionally get per-item disagreement scores for free.

The NaN masking matters — in our pilot pool each item is only annotated by 2 of 4 annotators, exactly the sparse pattern the release code expects.

Risk to flag: disagreement scores are well calibrated on political-speech items but noisy on slang-heavy ones, where annotator pools are small. Maren is pulling more annotations for those slices via Corpus before we call it robust. Also re-confirming: binary labels only for now.

Csilla
